Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | ${e}^{2}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot {\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{2} \\  & ={\frac{{u}^{2}}{3}|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{5}⁡(3x).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{x{log}_{5}⁡(3x)}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{{log}_{5}⁡(3x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡5\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡5\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡5\operatorname{ln}⁡|{log}_{5}⁡(3x)|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e$ | ${e}^{2}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e}^{{e}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x} & ={\int }_{e}^{{e}^{2}}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1 \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{4}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡4\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $4$ | $16$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{16}\frac{2}{x{log}_{4}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{1}{{log}_{4}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =2{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡4\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{2})\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\  & =4{ln}^{2}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{7}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡7}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡7\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{7}⁡x}{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int {log}_{7}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡7\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{2}\int u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{2}\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{4}\cdot {log}_{7}^{2}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$
